title: Add optimistic concurrency tokens to mutable aggregates
acceptance_criteria: Mutable aggregates (Session, VisibilityRule, PurchaseTransaction, Workspace, Participant, quota usage) carry a concurrency token (Postgres xmin) so a concurrent read-modify-write fails loudly instead of silently losing an update; a conflicting write returns 409/retry rather than overwriting.
required_tests: Integration: two interleaved updates to one Session (start vs end) and one VisibilityRule (reveal vs hide) - the second write detects the conflict; single-writer happy path unaffected.
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL (release blocker). A repo-wide search for RowVersion/IsRowVersion/IsConcurrencyToken/xmin returns ZERO matches in apps/api; Session and VisibilityRule are written with a bare Update+SaveChanges (SessionRepository.cs UpdateAsync ~143-154, VisibilityRuleRepository.cs UpdateAsync ~144-154). The CanStart/CanEnd state-machine guards are in-memory only and give no cross-DbContext/replica protection, so concurrent commands silently lose updates. Map the Postgres system column xmin as an EF concurrency token (Property<uint>(xmin).IsRowVersion().HasColumnName(xmin)) on the mutable aggregates and translate DbUpdateConcurrencyException to 409 on the endpoints. No data migration needed (xmin is a system column). Reuse the existing repositories; do not change their public contracts.

title: Wrap multi-step command handlers in a single transaction (unit of work)
acceptance_criteria: Each command that performs a rule/state change plus audit plus event-append plus quota change commits them in ONE database transaction; a part-way failure rolls everything back so the append-only event stream can never diverge from persisted state; realtime delivery happens after commit.
required_tests: Integration: inject a failure after the rule change but before the event append and assert NOTHING persisted (no orphan audit, no half-applied reveal); happy path persists every effect exactly once.
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL (release blocker). Today each repository call is its own SaveChangesAsync with no unit-of-work spanning a handler: RevealService.ApplyVisibilityChangeAsync commits the rule, then audit, then idempotency key as separate saves (RevealService.cs ~283-309), then the endpoint publishes 2-3 events each its own append (RevealEndpoints.cs ~271-335; SessionEventPublisher.PublishAsync appends then delivers ~69-108). Session start does session.Start -> UpdateAsync -> quota record -> audit -> publish separately (SessionEndpoints.cs ~563-595). A crash between steps leaves visibility changed with no ContentRevealed event (replay reconstructs a state the stream never recorded) or double audit/event on retry. Introduce an explicit transaction scope around the full handler for reveal/hide and session start/end/cancel; deliver realtime AFTER commit (commit-then-publish) so a delivery failure cannot roll back committed state. IMPLEMENT the transaction inside DbContext.Database.CreateExecutionStrategy().ExecuteAsync(async () => { BeginTransactionAsync ... CommitAsync }) - NOT a bare user-initiated BeginTransactionAsync - so it stays correct once CORE-CONC-003 enables EnableRetryOnFailure (a retrying execution strategy forbids user transactions outside ExecuteAsync); ExecuteAsync is equally correct with today's default non-retrying strategy. Reuse existing repositories.

title: Add database connection resilience (retry on transient failures)
acceptance_criteria: Transient Postgres failures (failover, restart, brief network partition, pool exhaustion) are retried automatically by EF/Npgsql instead of surfacing as request 5xx or worker-job exceptions; retry is enabled for the API and every worker job context.
required_tests: Integration/unit asserting the DbContext uses a retrying execution strategy; a simulated transient failure is retried and succeeds.
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL (release blocker, one-line-per-context fix). EnableRetryOnFailure is absent everywhere: Program.cs ~204 (UseNpgsql with no retry) and every worker job extension (AssetCleanupServiceCollectionExtensions.cs ~49, RecapGenerationServiceCollectionExtensions.cs ~52, ExportProcessingServiceCollectionExtensions.cs ~54, StoreNotificationReconciliationServiceCollectionExtensions.cs ~71, LiveCoreDbContextFactory.cs ~54). In the documented topology (API behind a proxy, Postgres as a separate service) a routine DB blip becomes user-facing 5xx and job failures. Add options.UseNpgsql(cs, o => o.EnableRetryOnFailure(...)) consistently. The CORE-CONC-002 transactional commands already run inside CreateExecutionStrategy().ExecuteAsync, so enabling retry is safe - but before enabling, verify no bare user-initiated BeginTransaction remains anywhere (a retrying strategy throws on those). Keep the fail-closed-when-unconfigured posture.

title: Make quota check-and-consume atomic (close the TOCTOU race)
acceptance_criteria: Two concurrent commands consuming the same quota cannot both pass the limit; the consume is a single atomic conditional update (or unique reservation) so session.active.max / workspace.active.max cannot be exceeded under a race.
required_tests: Concurrency test: N parallel session/start (or workspace/create) at a limit of 1 yield exactly 1 success and N-1 quota-exceeded.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH. QuotaEnforcementService does CheckAsync then RecordConsumptionAsync as separate non-transactional steps with no row lock or reserved increment - explicitly acknowledged as a follow-up (QuotaEnforcementService.cs ~30-32). Two concurrent session/start or workspace/create both read used<limit and both record. Replace with an atomic limit-guarded increment (UPDATE ... SET used = used + 1 WHERE used < limit RETURNING, or a unique reservation row) so check+consume is one statement. Reuse the Entitlements quota_usage table. Pairs with CORE-MON-005/006/007 which add the missing enforcement points.

title: Scope visibility rules and realtime fan-out to the session
acceptance_criteria: A reveal made in one session is visible ONLY within that session; a participant connected to a different concurrent session of the same workspace never receives or sees it (live delivery, replay, or visible-feed); visibility decisions and the realtime recipient set are bounded by sessionId.
required_tests: Integration (crown jewel): workspace W with two live sessions A and B with disjoint participants - a reveal in A is NOT delivered to and NOT in the feed/replay of B's participants; same-session participants still see it; foreign-tenant still 404.
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL (release blocker - the most severe security finding: cross-session data leak). VisibilityRule has OrganizationId/WorkspaceId/ResourceType/ResourceId/TargetParticipantId but NO SessionId (VisibilityRule.cs ~61-198, VisibilityRuleConfiguration.cs ~66-160), so VisibilityPolicy looks rules up workspace-wide (VisibilityPolicy.cs ~128-185) and SessionEventRecipientResolver fans out via ListActiveByWorkspaceAsync - all active participants of the WORKSPACE, not the session (SessionEventRecipientResolver.cs ~100-113, ParticipantRepository.cs ~97-127). Nothing forbids multiple concurrent sessions per workspace (SessionRepository.cs ~135-137). Add SessionId to VisibilityRule (+ migration + the documented index), thread it through RevealService/VisibilityPolicy, and change the recipient resolver to enumerate participants of the SESSION. DECISION + ADR: confirm reveals are session-scoped (recommended) vs any workspace-shared resource modeled explicitly. Update docs/10, docs/11, csv/database_tables.csv. Reuse VisibilityPolicy as the single decision point; do not fork the logic.

title: Prevent duplicate and ghost visibility rules (uniqueness and conflict handling)
acceptance_criteria: For a given (session, resource, dimension) at most one active visibility rule exists; a hide always fully reverses a prior reveal (no resource stays visible after a successful hide); concurrent first-reveals do not create two rules.
required_tests: Concurrency: two simultaneous first-reveals of one resource produce one rule not two; reveal-then-hide leaves the resource hidden even under a racing second reveal; idempotent double-hide.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH. The (workspace_id, resource_type, resource_id) index is deliberately NON-unique (VisibilityRuleConfiguration.cs ~116-120); EnsureStateAsync creates a new visible rule when it finds none (RevealService.cs ~374-394) so two concurrent first-reveals with different idempotency keys both AddAsync, and a later Hide flips only inDimension[0] (~374-381) leaving a second rule Visible -> an un-hideable ghost reveal. Add a unique constraint on (session_id, resource_type, resource_id, target_participant_id) (after CORE-SVIS-001 adds session_id) and use insert-on-conflict so the dimension has exactly one row. Depends on CORE-SVIS-001; benefits from CORE-CONC-001. Reuse RevealService + IdempotencyKeyStore.

title: Add a per-session monotonic event sequence
acceptance_criteria: Every session event carries a per-session, gap-free, strictly monotonic sequence number; replay and ordering use that sequence not the UUIDv7 id; events appended in the same millisecond preserve append order; a client detects a missed event by sequence gap.
required_tests: Append several events within one millisecond and assert read-back order equals append order; replay cursor after sequence N returns N+1.. with no skips/dupes; a missing sequence is detectable.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH. The stream is read OrderBy(e => e.Id) (SessionEventRepository.cs ~52-57) and SessionEvent.Create uses Guid.CreateVersion7() WITHOUT a timestamp (SessionEvent.cs ~286); UUIDv7 is only monotonic at millisecond resolution (the team already hit this - commits 8161ef6/c493446 - but fixed only the TESTS, not production). One reveal publishes ContentRevealed + VisibilityRuleChanged + SceneActivated at the same now (RevealEndpoints.cs ~278-334) so their order is random within the ms. Add a per-session sequence (a session_event_seq counter or a per-session DB sequence, allocated inside the CORE-CONC-002 transaction) and order/replay by (session_id, sequence). Update docs/11 and the SliceAfter cursor (SessionReplayService.cs ~145-167). Reuse the existing append path.

title: Re-authorize realtime connections on role change and participant removal
acceptance_criteria: When a participant is removed or a member is demoted mid-session, their existing live hub connection stops receiving events they are no longer authorized to see (eviction or per-send re-check), not only on reconnect.
required_tests: Integration: a participant removed mid-session receives no further events on the open socket; a demoted host loses host-group deliveries.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. SessionHub.OnConnectedAsync resolves groups once and joins them (SessionHub.cs ~58-104) with no re-authorization or eviction hook, so a removed participant's still-open connection stays in its groups and a demoted host keeps host/observer group sends (participant audience sends are re-gated per event by SessionEventRecipientResolver, but group membership is not). Add an eviction signal on Participant.Remove / member demotion (abort the connection or remove it from its groups) and/or re-check authorization at send time for host/observer groups. Reuse the connection resolver; do not widen any audience.

title: Reverse the v1 billing deferral in the specifications
acceptance_criteria: The specs declare billing/monetization IN SCOPE for v1; docs/01 and docs/24 (and the ENTL/STORE/ADS rows) no longer mark the purchase-to-entitlement grant chain as deferred; a single source of truth states the v1 monetization scope and acceptance.
required_tests: spec-consistency stays green; boundary scan clean; doc-only change (no Core source).
notes: TIER 1 (enabling, docs-only). Reverses CORE-DOC-002 which formally deferred the purchase->entitlement grant chain for v1 (commit 766ec75). docs/01_PRODUCT_VISION_AND_SCOPE.md lists billing as OUT-OF-SCOPE and docs/24 records the deferral, but the product now REQUIRES monetization in v1. Update docs/01, docs/21, docs/22, docs/24 and the annotated ENTL/STORE/ADS story rows to state billing is in-scope for v1 and define v1 acceptance (a verified purchase grants the buyer a SubjectEntitlement; refunds revoke; free-tier quotas enforced server-side). This story unblocks CORE-MON-002..010. Docs/csv only.

title: Add buyer linkage to verified purchases (billing_account_links)
acceptance_criteria: A verified purchase is durably linked to the authenticated buyer (subject) so it can later grant that subject an entitlement; the same external receipt cannot be claimed by two different subjects.
required_tests: Integration: a verified purchase records the buyer; user B cannot bind user A's transaction/receipt; foreign-tenant denied.
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL for monetization. PurchaseTransaction has NO subject/user/org column - the authenticated buyer is verified then discarded (PurchaseTransaction.cs ~26-29 NO BUYER COLUMN ... a later story; ApplePurchaseEndpoints.cs ~88-94/149-157 only RecordVerifiedPurchaseAsync), and the idempotency key (provider, provider_transaction_id) is global/user-independent so two users submitting the same receipt collapse to one row. Add the documented billing_account_links table (or a subject column on the purchase) linking purchase -> subject, with a uniqueness rule that a receipt maps to exactly one subject. Reuse the Store + Entitlements modules and the existing verify pipeline - this is the prerequisite the deferral named (docs/24 ~88-89). Update docs/10, csv/database_tables.csv, csv/entitlement_database_tables.csv. Fail-closed.

title: Implement the purchase to entitlement grant chain
acceptance_criteria: A successfully verified, buyer-linked purchase grants the buyer the corresponding SubjectEntitlement (the documented SKU -> entitlement mapping); the grant is idempotent and reflected in the effective-entitlements read.
required_tests: Integration: a verified purchase grants exactly the mapped entitlement to the buyer; a duplicate webhook/retry does not double-grant; an unverified/failed purchase grants nothing (fail-closed).
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL for monetization. The grant chain is deferred today: ApplePurchaseEndpoints (and Google) only RecordVerifiedPurchaseAsync; no SubjectEntitlement is assigned. Wire the existing verify-and-record pipeline to the entitlement assignment primitive (SubjectEntitlement / the assignment service already in Entitlements) using the product->entitlement mapping; make the grant idempotent on (purchase, entitlement). Depends on CORE-MON-002 (buyer linkage); do the record+grant in one transaction (CORE-CONC-002). Reuse SubjectEntitlementResolver and the assignment service; do not duplicate. Update csv/entitlement_event_catalog.csv (EntitlementGranted now real). Fail-closed.

title: Make the purchase status machine monotonic (refunds revoke and stay revoked)
acceptance_criteria: A refunded/cancelled/charged-back purchase revokes the granted entitlement and CANNOT be reactivated by a later renewal/notification; a revoked state is terminal (absorbing).
required_tests: A Refunded purchase followed by a later-OccurredAt Renewed notification stays Refunded and the entitlement stays revoked; reconciliation cannot resurrect it.
notes: TIER 1 CRITICAL for monetization (revenue/security). PurchaseTransaction.ChangeStatus allows ANY transition (PurchaseTransaction.cs ~166-181, only short-circuits when newStatus==Status); StoreNotificationService maps Renewed->Active and applies unconditionally (~100-108), and reconciliation drives the purchase to the AppliedStatus of the latest-OccurredAt notification (~188-190, ReconcilablePurchaseReader.cs ~99-118). A legitimate DID_RENEW with a later event time than a refund flips Refunded->Active = free premium once granting is live (violates docs/21 refund-revocation). Add an explicit state machine making Refunded/Cancelled/Chargeback absorbing; on entering a revoked state revoke the granted entitlement (ties to CORE-MON-003). Also validate StoreNotification.OccurredAt (reject default/absurd-future, StoreNotification.cs ~87-113). Reuse the existing services.

title: Enforce session.participant.max server-side
acceptance_criteria: A participant join is rejected when the session is at its plan participant limit (the documented free-tier gate); enforcement is server-side not UI-only; concurrent joins cannot exceed the limit.
required_tests: Join at the limit is rejected (quota-exceeded); concurrent joins at limit-1 admit exactly the remaining slots; a paid plan allows more.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH for monetization. Only WorkspaceActiveMax and SessionActiveMax are enforced keys (QuotaEntitlementKeys.cs ~24,33); the participant-join path (SessionParticipantJoinService.JoinAsync) performs NO quota check, so the headline free-tier participant cap is UI-only and trivially bypassed - the exact failure docs/21 says Core exists to prevent. Add a session.participant.max quota key and enforce it in the join flow via QuotaEnforcementService (atomic per CORE-CONC-004). The JoinAsync service already exists (it just has no production caller yet - CORE-PRS-001 wires that), so the check and its test can be added here against the service. Reuse the entitlements quota services. Update csv/mobile_entitlement_catalog.csv / docs/21 if the key name is new. Fail-closed.

title: Enforce asset.storage.bytes.max on upload
acceptance_criteria: An asset upload is rejected when the workspace/subject would exceed its plan storage quota; enforcement is server-side at upload-intent; freeing assets restores headroom.
required_tests: Upload over quota rejected; under quota succeeds; deleting an asset restores available bytes.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH for monetization. No storage key exists in QuotaEntitlementKeys and AssetUploadIntentService / AssetEndpoints.CreateUploadIntentAsync does no quota check, so free users have unbounded storage. Add asset.storage.bytes.max, track consumed bytes per workspace/subject, and enforce at upload-intent (consume) and asset deletion (release), atomically (CORE-CONC-004). Reuse the Assets + Entitlements modules. Update docs/21 / the entitlement catalog. Fail-closed; 503 if storage unconfigured.

title: Release workspace.active.max quota on archive
acceptance_criteria: Archiving a workspace releases its workspace.active.max consumption so the count tracks actual active workspaces; a free user who archives can create again; create still consumes; release is idempotent.
required_tests: Create then archive then create succeeds at limit 1; quota_usage returns to 0 after archive; double-archive does not double-release.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH for monetization (correctness/UX, lost revenue + support load). WorkspaceEndpoints.cs ~255-262 records consumption on create but ArchiveWorkspaceAsync (~430-510) performs NO QuotaEnforcement.ReleaseAsync, unlike the symmetric session start/end (SessionEndpoints.cs ~612-617); the active-list query excludes archived workspaces (WorkspaceRepository.cs ~104-106) so quota_usage drifts permanently up and a free user (limit 1) is locked out forever after create->archive. Add a ReleaseAsync on archive mirroring session end; make it idempotent. Reuse the quota services.

title: Receipt verification adapter contract: fail-closed, sandbox/prod separation, replay protection
acceptance_criteria: Apple/Google receipt verification is delegated to a deployment-supplied adapter behind a fail-closed port that distinguishes sandbox vs production and rejects replayed receipts; Core never trusts client-asserted purchase state and ships no provider keys.
required_tests: Unconfigured adapter -> fail-closed (503/422, no grant); a replayed receipt is rejected/idempotent; a sandbox receipt is not honored in production.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH for monetization (security). The verify gate already delegates to deployment adapters and fails closed (good). As part of enabling v1 billing, make the adapter contract explicit for sandbox/prod separation and receipt-replay protection, and add the negative tests Core can own (a forged-sentinel rejection exists; add replay + sandbox/prod). The cryptographic verification itself is adapter-supplied (out of Core per T7/docs/13) - Core guarantees fail-closed without it. Reuse the existing verifier ports; document the adapter requirements in docs/13. Do NOT embed provider SDKs/keys in Core.

title: Implement the mobile /v1 entitlements and purchase route shape
acceptance_criteria: A buyer can read their effective entitlements over the documented mobile path; the mobile-facing /v1/... path shape resolves to the implemented /api/v1 endpoints (gateway/rewrite implemented or documented as the contract); authorized and tenant-scoped.
required_tests: Authenticated read returns the caller's effective entitlements; anonymous 401; the documented mobile path reaches the endpoint (no 404).
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM for monetization. csv/mobile_store_api_routes.csv documents /v1/me/entitlements and /v1/purchases/apple/transactions but endpoints are mounted at /api/v1 (MeEntitlementsEndpoints.cs ~58, ApplePurchaseEndpoints.cs ~64) with no in-repo rewrite, so a mobile client following the CSV literally 404s. Either implement the /v1 path shape (gateway/route prefix) or reconcile the CSV + document the rewrite as the contract. Reuse SubjectEntitlementResolver / EffectiveEntitlement. NOTE CORE-API-007 may already cover /api/v1/me/entitlements - check git history and extend rather than duplicate.

title: Make store-notification handling atomic (status change and dedup ledger in one transaction)
acceptance_criteria: Applying a store notification (purchase status change) and writing its dedup ledger row happen in one transaction so a crash cannot leave a status applied without its first-arrival record and a re-delivery cannot double-append the purchase_events audit trail.
required_tests: Inject a failure between status change and ledger write -> neither persists; replay of the same notificationUUID is a no-op; out-of-order delivery converges correctly.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM for monetization. HandleAsync commits ChangeStatusAsync (its own SaveChanges via PurchaseTransactionRepository.UpdateAsync) and only THEN inserts the store_notification_events dedup row (StoreNotificationService.cs ~101-123) in separate transactions; a crash between leaves the status changed but the notification unrecorded -> re-delivery re-applies and can duplicate the purchase_events entry. Wrap apply+ledger in one transaction (uses CORE-CONC-002). Reuse StoreNotificationService. Also document the scale follow-up: ReconcilablePurchaseReader computes latest-per-purchase in memory (~83-109) - fine for the off-by-default low-volume job.

title: Prevent duplicate recaps under concurrent workers
acceptance_criteria: At most one system recap exists per session regardless of how many worker replicas or overlapping sweeps run; a second concurrent sweep produces no duplicate.
required_tests: Two concurrent recap sweeps over the same eligible session produce exactly one recap; a sequential re-sweep is a no-op.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (multi-worker correctness). Eligibility is a NOT EXISTS read (RecapEligibleSessionReader.cs ~44-56) fully decoupled from the bare Add+SaveChanges (RecapRepository.cs ~22-28); the only recaps indexes are non-unique (RecapConfiguration.cs ~106-116) and each GenerateBySystem mints a fresh UUIDv7 PK so both inserts succeed; the worker hosted service has no single-instance guard (WorkerHostFactory.cs ~98-100). Add a unique (partial) index on recaps(session_id) for system recaps + insert-on-conflict handling, and/or claim sessions with a lease/SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Update docs/10, csv/database_tables.csv. Reuse the Recap aggregate.

title: Generate recaps from the session event stream
acceptance_criteria: A generated recap reflects what actually happened in the session (derived from session_events) not just the start/end timestamps; empty/partial streams are handled safely and deterministically.
required_tests: A session with reveals/scene activations produces a recap summarizing those events; a zero-event session produces a safe empty recap; non-UTC/edge timestamps handled.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (the stated recaps-from-the-event-stream goal is not implemented). ComposeSummary consumes only session.StartedAt/EndedAt (RecapGenerationService.cs ~152-167) and RecapEligibleSession carries only the two timestamps (RecapEligibleSession.cs ~24-29); no file under apps/api/Recaps reads session_events, so recaps are content-free boilerplate. Read the session event stream (visibility-safe projection) to compose the recap, keeping it deterministic. If Core deliberately leaves rich recap content to a vertical, instead make that explicit in docs and downgrade the scope - decide and document. Reuse SessionEventRepository + RecapProjection (which already fails closed, RecapProjection.cs ~147-166). Pairs with CORE-TST-005.

title: Implement the participant join/leave flow that emits ParticipantJoined/Left
acceptance_criteria: A participant joining or leaving a session actually triggers ParticipantJoined/ParticipantLeft emission to authorized recipients (presence works end-to-end); payloads are identifier-only (no PII).
required_tests: Integration: join then leave persist one event each, are delivered to hosts/observers, contain no display names/PII; foreign-tenant/unauthorized denied.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (presence does not work at go-live; 2 of 8 live events are dead code). SessionParticipantJoinService.JoinAsync and SessionParticipantLeaveService.LeaveAsync are DI-registered (Program.cs ~543,552) but have NO production caller (grep of .JoinAsync(/.LeaveAsync( finds only DI + tests), SessionHub exposes no client-callable methods (SessionHub.cs ~31-33), and there is no HTTP join/leave route in csv/api_routes.csv. Wire a real entry point: an HTTP join/leave route or hub OnConnected/OnDisconnected (re-using the admission/leave services) so the documented ParticipantJoined/ParticipantLeft (event catalog) actually fire. NOTE CORE-EVT-002 added the emission but left it unreachable - this story adds the missing caller. The session.participant.max quota enforced in CORE-MON-005 now applies on this real path. Keep payloads PII-free (T7). Update csv/api_routes.csv if a route is added.

title: Add rate limiting (anonymous webhooks and global)
acceptance_criteria: The application enforces rate limits: a strict per-IP limit on the anonymous store-notification webhooks and a per-principal global limiter on authenticated endpoints; excess requests get 429; limits are configurable.
required_tests: Integration: the anonymous webhook returns 429 past the threshold; an authenticated principal is throttled past its limit; normal traffic unaffected.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (independently flagged by 3 audit dimensions). No rate limiting anywhere - grep for RateLimit/AddRateLimiter/UseRateLimiter returns zero (Program.cs pipeline ~886-1239). The two AllowAnonymous webhooks POST /api/v1/store-notifications/{apple,google/rtdn} (StoreNotificationEndpoints.cs ~51-59) do DB work and run an external parser per call - a clear abuse/DoS and ledger-amplification surface; also invite-token / organizationSlug enumeration. Add ASP.NET Core rate limiting (UseRateLimiter): per-IP fixed/sliding window on the webhooks (plus a hard body-size cap beyond MaxRawPayloadLength), per-principal global limiter elsewhere. Configurable. No new heavy dependency (built-in).

title: Implement the view-audit-log read endpoint
acceptance_criteria: An Owner/Admin/Auditor can read their tenant's audit log over HTTP (the capability the authorization matrix grants); results are tenant-scoped and paged; unauthorized roles and foreign tenants are denied.
required_tests: Integration: Auditor reads the audit log; a non-privileged role 403; foreign-tenant 404/empty; a PII/secret-free projection.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH. docs/06 + csv/authorization_matrix.csv grant Owner/Admin/Auditor view-audit-log and AuditQueryPolicy + AuditLogEntryView exist and are unit-tested, but csv/api_routes.csv defines NO audit route and none is mapped - the audit log is write-only and the Auditor role cannot fulfill its sole purpose. Add GET /api/v1/audit-logs (tenant-scoped, paged) on top of the existing AuditQueryPolicy. Reuse the policy + view; do not expose other tenants; keep the projection PII/secret-free (T7). Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08.

title: Make the audit log tamper-evident
acceptance_criteria: Audit log entries are tamper-evident (a per-tenant hash chain linking each entry to the previous) and/or the DB role denies UPDATE/DELETE on audit_logs so silent alteration of history is detectable/prevented.
required_tests: Tampering with a persisted entry breaks chain verification; the verifier passes on an untampered chain.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (hardening). AuditLogRepository exposes only AppendAsync + read and AuditLogEntry is immutable (good app-level append-only), but there is no hash chain / sequence signing / DB write-once, so a DB-level actor or a future regression could alter/delete rows undetected. Add a prev-hash column forming a per-tenant chain plus a verification routine, and/or document a deployment step to REVOKE UPDATE/DELETE on audit_logs. Reuse the existing append path; do not change the read contract.

title: Encrypt backups at rest
acceptance_criteria: The backup tooling encrypts the Postgres dump and mirrored assets at rest (or refuses to run without an encryption sink); the most sensitive data (audit, purchase ledger, tenant data) never lands as plaintext by default.
required_tests: The backup script produces an encrypted artifact (or fails closed when no key/recipient is configured); restore decrypts and round-trips.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH. docs/13 ~667 mandates Encrypt backups at rest and in transit but backup-livecore.ps1 ~134 writes a plaintext pg_dump custom-format file and plaintext mirrored assets with no encrypt step (grep encrypt/gpg/age in scripts finds none); the dump holds the audit trail, purchase ledger and all tenant data. Add an encryption sink (age/gpg or storage SSE) to backup-livecore.ps1 / LiveCoreBackup.psm1 and the matching decrypt to restore-livecore.ps1; fail-closed when unconfigured. Reuse the existing scripts. Update docs/13.

title: Test the real backup/restore path in CI against live Postgres
acceptance_criteria: CI exercises the ACTUAL backup-livecore.ps1 / restore-livecore.ps1 (real pg_dump/pg_restore/psql) against a real Postgres, asserting a full backup -> restore -> integrity round-trip, not just a fixture.
required_tests: A CI job backs up a seeded Postgres, restores into a fresh database, and the to_jsonb integrity/row-count checks pass.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH. The CI backup-restore-drill job runs only test-backup-restore-drill.ps1 which needs no database or object store (in-memory fixture, scripts/test-backup-restore-drill.ps1 ~11,20); the real scripts that invoke pg_dump/pg_restore/psql and the to_jsonb checksum (backup-livecore.ps1 ~150, restore-livecore.ps1 ~153) are never run in CI, so a broken argument would ship green and RTO/RPO claims rest on an untested path. Add a CI job using the Postgres service the migrations/integration-postgres jobs already spin up to run the real backup+restore round-trip. Update .github/workflows/ci.yml.

title: Expose worker job-failure metrics and per-job health
acceptance_criteria: The worker exposes its metrics (the livecore_job_failures_total counters already recorded) via a scrape/OTLP endpoint, and liveness distinguishes the four job loops so one hung loop is detectable.
required_tests: The worker metrics endpoint responds and reflects a forced job failure; a stalled single loop is detectable via per-job heartbeat.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (monitoring blind spot on the host doing irreversible work). All four worker loops call RecordBackgroundJobFailure (AssetCleanupBackgroundService.cs ~123, RecapGenerationBackgroundService.cs ~118, StoreNotificationReconciliationBackgroundService.cs ~126, export processing) but WorkerHostFactory.cs ~56-61 registers metrics with no scrape/OTLP endpoint, and one shared heartbeat file (~89-90) means one healthy loop masks three hung ones. Add a metrics surface (OTLP export or a lightweight scrape port) and per-loop heartbeat/health. Reuse the existing meter; mirror the API observability wiring. Update docs/15 (and CORE-OPS-005 heartbeat doc, which omits the export + store-reconciliation loops).

title: Document the migration rollback and expand-contract story
acceptance_criteria: There is a documented backward path for a bad deploy (roll-forward-only + restore-from-backup, or a tested down path) and expand/contract guidance so destructive Down() migrations are not run blindly; the runbook states the chosen policy.
required_tests: Doc-driven; optionally a CI lint/test that a Down() dropping a column is flagged for review.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. The Migrations.Dockerfile only applies forward (efbundle entrypoint, ~76) and every Down() is destructive (e.g. AddWorkspaceStatus drops the status column ~38-43; ~32 migrations have DropColumn in Down) with no rollback procedure or zero-downtime guidance in docs/13. Document the policy (recommended: roll-forward-only + restore-from-backup, with expand/contract for schema changes) so operators do not discover it during an incident. Docs-only (plus optional CI lint of destructive Downs).

title: Ship in-repo deployment manifests
acceptance_criteria: The repo contains a runnable docker-compose (and/or Helm chart) wiring API + worker + Postgres with the migrate-before-API gate and the documented health/readiness/liveness probes, so an operator can deploy from this repo alone.
required_tests: A CI smoke that the compose/Helm renders/starts and the migrate gate blocks API start until migrations complete.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM. No docker-compose/Helm exists in-repo; README defers all orchestration to a separate livecore-deploy repo, so self-hostable from the beginning (docs/13) is only half true and the two easiest-to-get-wrong pieces (migrate-before-api ordering via depends_on: service_completed_successfully, and the heartbeat liveness probe) exist only as prose. Add a minimal, tested compose (and optionally a Helm chart) using the existing API/worker/migrations images. Reuse the documented env contract. Update docs/13. Also reconcile .env.example which omits Store:Reconciliation:Enabled, Assets:Cleanup:* and Tracing:Otlp sampling keys the code reads.

title: Graceful shutdown/drain and SignalR sticky-session posture
acceptance_criteria: Both hosts drain in-flight HTTP/SignalR connections on shutdown within a tuned window; the docs state the multi-instance SignalR sticky-session/affinity requirement for the negotiate/transport handshake.
required_tests: A rolling restart does not abruptly cut an in-flight request; the docs state the sticky-session requirement.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. Grep for ShutdownTimeout/HostOptions returns nothing - both hosts use framework defaults; worker loops honor cancellation (good) but there is no tuned drain window and nothing documents that a multi-instance SignalR deployment needs sticky sessions/ARR affinity (only the Redis backplane is documented, CORE-OPS-007) - non-WebSocket fallback breaks negotiation without affinity. Tune HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout and document the sticky-session requirement in docs/13. Small code + docs.

title: Pin base images and add SBOM and vulnerability scan to publish
acceptance_criteria: Published images pin their base image by digest, a CVE scan runs and can fail the publish on critical vulnerabilities, and an SBOM is produced; the existing immutable LiveCore tag guard stays.
required_tests: CI publish dry-run produces an SBOM and a scan report; a seeded critical CVE fails the gate.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (supply chain). The publish job builds/pushes by version tag but base images float (mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0, aspnet:10.0 in all three Dockerfiles) with no digest pin, no docker scout/Trivy/Grype, no SBOM/provenance (ci.yml ~383-401); the immutability guard protects the published tag but the underlying layers drift and no gate catches a known-CVE base image. Pin base images by digest, add an image scan + SBOM (and optionally cosign provenance) to the publish job. Update .github/workflows/ci.yml and the Dockerfiles. Also enforce dotnet restore --locked-mode (packages.lock.json) for reproducibility.

title: Make the spec-consistency check validate semantics not just names
acceptance_criteria: spec-consistency.ps1 validates route roles/auth and CSV-routes-against-implemented-endpoints (both directions), the entitlement event catalog, the mobile store CSV, and table columns/indexes - not only name/count set-membership; CI fails on semantic drift.
required_tests: Seeded drift (a route with a changed role; an undocumented endpoint; an entitlement-catalog event with no audit action) fails the check; the real tree passes.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. scripts/spec-consistency.ps1 checks 5 string-set invariants only (~106-199): it does NOT validate route roles/auth_required, CSV routes vs actual endpoints, the entitlement event catalog, the mobile store CSV, or any column/index/constraint, and it never checks emission reachability - so a green Spec consistency passed gives false confidence (auth-role drift, undocumented routes, dead events all pass; e.g. ParticipantJoined/Left are documented live but unreachable). Extend the checks to cover those. Reuse the EF model snapshot + the minimal-API registrations for the code side. Script + docs/24 only.

title: Back the entitlement/store event catalog with real audit actions
acceptance_criteria: Every entitlement/store event the catalog marks audit=true (EntitlementGranted/Revoked, QuotaExceeded, PurchaseVerification*, StoreNotification*) is actually persisted/audited via a real AuditAction; the catalog is a contract not aspirational.
required_tests: Granting/revoking an entitlement, a quota denial, and a store-notification apply each write the documented audit record; the catalog matches the AuditAction enum.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM. csv/entitlement_event_catalog.csv marks those events persisted+audited, but AuditAction.cs ~24-176 contains only 11 actions, none entitlement/store/purchase, and QuotaExceeded exists only as an HTTP-429 helper name (WorkspaceEndpoints.cs ~873) - the catalog is aspirational and spec-consistency does not check it. Add the missing AuditAction values and emit them on grant/revoke/quota-denial/notification-apply (ties to CORE-MON-003/004). Reuse the Audit module append path. Update the catalog/docs to match what is actually emitted.

title: Add coverage measurement and a CI gate
acceptance_criteria: CI collects code coverage and reports it; a threshold (start non-blocking, then blocking) prevents a new untested production handler from silently regressing coverage.
required_tests: The CI run produces a coverage report; a deliberately-untested new handler trips the threshold once blocking is enabled.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (the strong coverage is unguarded). coverlet.collector is referenced in all three test csproj but no CI step or csproj passes --collect/CollectCoverage/threshold (ci.yml ~54,337) - coverage is computed nowhere and gates nothing, so DoD no-feature-without-tests rests on author discipline only and can silently regress. Add coverage collection (coverlet) + a report (and a threshold, initially warn-only) to ci.yml. Update docs/14 and docs/17.

title: Add a real SignalR HubConnection delivery and denial test
acceptance_criteria: An integration test opens a real SignalR HubConnection and asserts an authorized client RECEIVES a reveal payload and an unauthorized/foreign client is DENIED at connect/group level - exercising the actual transport, not a fake backplane.
required_tests: Authorized participant receives the event; a participant connecting with another participant's id is aborted; a cross-session participant receives nothing (with CORE-SVIS-001).
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (the product's core live mechanism is unverified end-to-end). RealtimeHubAuthenticationTests only tests the /negotiate auth gate; RealtimeDeliveryEndpointTests substitutes a RecordingRealtimeBackplane and asserts group NAMES (~221-260), never a real HubConnection receiving/being denied a payload. Add a test using HubConnectionBuilder against the test host. Reuse the existing test factory. Exercises the RealtimeConnectionResolver group authz (~161-167) at the HTTP level.

title: Add a Redis/Valkey backplane propagation test
acceptance_criteria: A test verifies that with the Redis/Valkey backplane configured, an event published on one API instance reaches a client connected to another instance, and channel-prefix isolation holds.
required_tests: Cross-instance fan-out delivers; a different ChannelPrefix does not leak.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (the documented production HA path is config-tested only). InProcessRealtimeBackplane is unit-tested; RealtimeServiceCollectionExtensionsTests only asserts DI wiring that AddStackExchangeRedis is registered when configured - no pub/sub, no cross-instance propagation, no failover. Add a behavioral test (Testcontainers Redis or a CI Redis service) for cross-instance delivery. Reuse the backplane registration; do not widen the audience.

title: Run unit/smoke against Postgres and fix the mislabeled CI step
acceptance_criteria: The unit and smoke suites also run against real Postgres (not only SQLite) so provider-specific behavior is exercised; the CI step that actually runs the whole solution is named correctly.
required_tests: A provider-divergent repository test passes on Postgres; the CI step names match what they run.

Provider-specific behaviour (collation, case-sensitivity, JSON, concurrency semantics) in unit-level repo tests is never exercised on Postgres. Run the unit/smoke suites against Postgres too (a CI matrix leg) and rename the mislabeled step. Update ci.yml.

title: Add recap content tests and de-flake the tracing absence assertion
acceptance_criteria: Recap summary content + edge cases (null StartedAt, zero-length session, non-UTC offsets) are tested; the timing-dependent tracing test uses a bounded poll instead of a fixed delay.

Add recap content/edge tests (pairs with CORE-RCP-002) and convert the delay to the bounded poll pattern already used by WaitForTraceAsync (~174-191). Tests only.

title: Provide an AGPL section 13 source-offer surface
acceptance_criteria: The network application offers remote users access to its Corresponding Source (an /about or /source endpoint/link exposing the version + source URL), satisfying AGPL-3.0 section 13 for a hosted deployment.
required_tests: Integration: the source-offer endpoint returns the source location + build version; no auth required.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (license compliance). The app is AGPL-3.0-or-later and network-interactive (SignalR hub + /api/v1), triggering AGPL section 13's obligation to offer remote users the Corresponding Source, but no /source//about/source-link endpoint exists (only the verbatim LICENSE text). Add a small anonymous endpoint exposing the source URL + build version. Reuse the VERSION constants. Update docs/16. No PII/secret.

title: Justify or replace the beta dependency and lock dependency restore
acceptance_criteria: The pre-release OpenTelemetry Prometheus exporter is either replaced with a stable release or explicitly justified per AGENTS.md, and container restore uses locked-mode so a published image's dependency closure matches what CI tested.

Also Dockerfiles run dotnet restore with no packages.lock.json/--locked-mode. Add the AGENTS.md-required justification and enforce locked restore. csproj + Dockerfile + docs.

title: Enforce cross-package version lockstep and tag-version consistency
acceptance_criteria: A test enforces that the four TS packages share one version (package.json + exported VERSION + per-package CHANGELOG + root CHANGELOG agree), and the release pipeline asserts the published image/release tag matches the intended package version; drift cannot ship.
required_tests: A seeded one-package version bump fails the lockstep test; a release tag mismatching the package version fails the publish gate.
notes: TIER 4 LOW. Each packages/*/tests/*.build.test.mjs checks only its OWN version triple; no test compares the four packages to each other or to root CHANGELOG.md, so bumping one package to 0.2.0 with the others at 0.1.0 still passes (docs/23 mandates a single shared version) - the fail-closed guarantee is weaker than stated. And ci.yml derives image tags from the git ref with nothing asserting the tag equals the packages' version. Add a cross-package lockstep test and a tag-vs-version gate (hosts are versioned separately from packages by design - assert the intended relationship). Reuse the existing build tests.

title: Close the brand-term scanner gap and neutralize leaked comments
acceptance_criteria: The boundary scanner can detect the forbidden brand/platform terms (ArcanOS, ScenarioOS, Enterprise, DnD, Pen-and-Paper), scans tracked source plus .Dockerfile, excludes gitignored tooling and the documentation files that legitimately list the terms, and the 4 ArcanOS source comments are neutralized; CI fails on any future brand leak in tracked source.
required_tests: boundary-scan.ps1 flags a seeded ArcanOS occurrence in a tracked .cs and in Migrations.Dockerfile; the gitignored scripts/story-loop.ps1 is NOT flagged; README.md/AGENTS.md are NOT flagged; the real tree scans clean after the fix.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (the non-negotiable product-neutrality rule is only half-enforced). PLACED LAST on purpose: it tightens the scanner, so it must run after every other story. Today csv/forbidden_core_terms.csv omits arcanos/scenarioos/enterprise/dnd/pen-and-paper that AGENTS.md:9 + docs/04 forbid, so the scanner cannot catch them - and ArcanOS leaked into 4 XML-doc comments: apps/api/Entitlements/EffectiveEntitlement.cs:14, EntitlementDefinition.cs:21, EntitlementSubjectType.cs:13, QuotaUnit.cs:12 (ArcanOS may display these as ...). Fix together: (a) add the brand terms to csv/forbidden_core_terms.csv keeping docs/ csv/ README.md AGENTS.md as the only allowed locations; (b) make the scanner enumerate TRACKED files only (git ls-files) so gitignored tooling (scripts/story-loop.ps1) is excluded, add .Dockerfile to scope, and explicitly exclude the documentation root files (README.md, AGENTS.md, LICENSE, CHANGELOG.md) that legitimately list the terms; (c) replace the 4 ArcanOS may display these as ... comments with a neutral a vertical may display these as .... Confirmed the only tracked source hits are those 4 files (no Enterprise/ScenarioOS/DnD in tracked apps/packages/tests/.github source). Keep the scanner fail-closed.
